summary: Sudden autoscale stutter causing reserved-pool throughput dips from ephemeral prober flood
description: Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-12 09:17 PDT, Nimbus AI reported recurring p95/p99 latency spikes and 429s on a set of batched routes served from their Dedicated reserved pool. Impact: customer-facing throughput dropped ~35% for 12-18 minute windows, causing downstream timeouts and >5% request failure rate for their primary chat endpoint. Environment: Dedicated reserved pool (customer: Nimbus AI, prod-us-west). Initial symptom pattern looks like autoscaler briefly shrinking capacity or delaying attachments, followed by rapid attach/fallback churn and transient GPU shortages.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Send sustained medium-concurrency traffic to customer's batched route (/v1/generate) with average payloads (~512 tokens) during a 10m window.
2) Observe that around t0+6m the autoscaler reports a brief shrink event, attach latencies increase and request 429s appear.
3) Repeat traffic while enabling sidecar debug to capture prober/healthcheck frequency.
4) Reproduce only observed on dedicated pool with specific tenant traffic mix (many short keepalive streams + periodic health probers).
logs: 2026-03-12T09:16:58Z allocator: scheduling: reserved-pool attach latency median=85ms p99=2.1s
2026-03-12T09:17:20Z sidecar-prober: probe /health freq=0.5s -> connections spike to 1.2k
2026-03-12T09:17:45Z api-gateway: response 429 route=/v1/generate tenant=nimbus-a count=73 window=30s
comments: Support (Ava Chen) 2026-03-12T09:32: Sent initial triage to SRE channel #incidents with sample logs and customer timeline. Asked Nimbus for traffic dump and confirmed this was not a usage spike from their app.

SRE (Marcus Lee) 2026-03-12T09:45: Noted a clustered burst of 0.5s-frequency health probes from a Nimbus sidecar process coinciding with autoscaler shrink decisions. Hypothesis: prober flood masquerading as legitimate small streams causing allocator to mark heartbeats and reduce perceived demand during scale_down cooldowns.

Customer (Nimbus Ops, Priya Shah) 2026-03-12T10:02: Confirmed a recent rollout of an internal monitoring agent that increased health-check frequency for internal containers. We will temporarily disable it on canary nodes.
SRE (Marcus Lee) 2026-03-12T10:15: Applied temporary mitigation: enforce per-tenant sidecar probe rate-limit at the edge and increased reserved-pool headroom by +2 replicas. Monitoring for stability.

Support (Ava Chen) 2026-03-12T11:20: Noted throughput recovered to baseline after mitigation; customer still sees occasional p95 blips during midday. Keeping ticket open to validate root cause and implement durable fix.
investigation_notes: Observation 1: Autoscaler shrink decisions occurred during windows where connection counts transiently dropped in our metrics, consistent with customer sidecars opening/closing many short-lived probes.
Observation 2: Sidecar prober traffic pattern shows tight polling (300-700ms) across many client hosts -> aggregated fanout to reserved pool gateways produced ephemeral connection churn.

Hypothesis: Aggregated health probe fanout creates short-lived connections that our allocator treats as low-utilization signals, triggering scale-down cooldown decisions; immediately after, attach latencies spike because of the subsequent rapid reconnects and KV-cache warmup costs.
Test executed: Enabled per-tenant probe rate limiting at gateway (0.2s min interval); reproduced load in staging and observed removal of autoscaler shrink events and 429s under synthetic probe flood.
Telemetry: p50 attach latency improved from 120ms->70ms, p99 attach from 2.1s->600ms in the test window after rate-limiting. KV cache miss rate reduced by ~18%.
resolution_summary: Temporary mitigations applied: 1) Edge rate-limit for health probes per tenant; 2) Increased reserved pool headroom for Nimbus by +2 replicas to reduce attach pressure; 3) Autoscaler config adjusted: extend scale_down cooldown for dedicated pools by +60s for this tenant only. Customer reverted their monitoring agent rollout on canary nodes. Result: throughput returned to baseline and 429s dropped to <0.2%
follow_up_actions: 1) SRE to implement a global per-tenant probe policing rule in gateway to avoid future prober floods (owner: Marcus Lee, due: 2026-03-18).
2) Product to consider exposing a per-tenant probe policy and guidance in docs for Dedicated customers (owner: Priya Desai, due: 2026-04-02).

3) Engineering to evaluate autoscaler heuristics to differentiate short-lived probe connections from true client load signals (owner: Scheduler Team, PR drafted: https://github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler/pull/998).
4) Runbook update: add a section for "ephemeral-prober flood" detection thresholds and remediation steps (owner: SRE).
5) Customer follow-up call scheduled to review mitigations and get confirmation of production stability (contact: Priya Shah, 2026-03-14 10:00 PDT).
